nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: The only caller: every read and every write of a board comes through it

nodes.name: Address and locate
nodes.responsibility: Maps names to safe vault paths
nodes.description: semanticBoardAddress normalizes board identity without I/O; locateSemanticBoard resolves the .semantic.json file and follows existing ancestors to refuse symlink paths that leave the configured vault.

nodes.name: List boards
nodes.responsibility: Discovers semantic board files
nodes.description: Recursively enumerates semantic board locations to a bounded depth, recognizing only .semantic.json aggregates and preserving their nested board names.

nodes.name: Read and validate
nodes.responsibility: Reads a coherent aggregate from disk, by its name or a name it used to have
nodes.description: readSemanticBoard asks Former names which board a name answers to; readSemanticBoardAt synchronously reads fresh bytes, parses JSON into the shared semantic schema, distinguishes missing from unreadable files, and rejects a document whose internal name disagrees with its address. A document of an older contract is migrated, and persisted when its lease is free, before it is answered.

nodes.name: Lifecycle transitions
nodes.responsibility: Defines board lifecycle changes
nodes.description: Factories return pure create, edit, branch, settle, adopt and shelve transitions; a rename is its own transition. The write boundary executes the chosen transition against the board read under lease.

nodes.name: Edit semantic content
nodes.responsibility: Resolves names into stable subjects
nodes.description: editContent, editViews, and editWalkthroughs plan removals, mint identifiers centrally, resolve same-write handles and references, preserve replacement semantics, and refuse orphaned containment or stranded narrative references.

nodes.name: Propagate descendant edits
nodes.responsibility: Carries parent changes into drafts
nodes.description: propagateEdit walks descendants of an edited variant, automatically merges compatible changes, records reconciliation issues where meanings diverge, and blocks descendants behind unresolved ancestors.

nodes.name: Settle disagreements
nodes.responsibility: Answers the disagreements a proposal holds and carries the answer down
nodes.description: settleVariant applies explicit reconciliation choices and ordering decisions; an ordinary edit that restores what a proposal removed settles through the same catch-up. A draft waiting on the answer is merged in the same write and reports what it finds.

nodes.name: Write under lease
nodes.responsibility: Commits one durable version
nodes.description: writeSemanticBoard locates the target, acquires the board-wide claim/lease, reads and validates under that lease, checks the expected version, applies one transition, validates the candidate, advances once, and persists once.

nodes.name: Atomic file replacement
nodes.responsibility: Fsyncs every change to a board file: a replacement, a move and an unlink
nodes.description: writeFileAtomic writes a temporary sibling, fsyncs file content, renames it over the destination, and fsyncs the directory; moveFileDurably and unlinkDurably sync the directory the same way, so accepted board writes are committed before callers receive success.

nodes.name: Vault diagnostics
nodes.responsibility: Everything wrong with the vault's boards, as warnings a repair can answer

nodes.name: Drill-down checks
nodes.responsibility: What a board can say about a link to another one, checked across the whole vault
nodes.description: A link is the one thing on a board that names something outside it, so no single board can check it: a node with nothing but its link, a board the vault does not hold, and a kind that disagrees with the level it opens (ADR 0029).

nodes.name: Replaced relationships
nodes.responsibility: Warns when a write may have lost a relationship's identity: re-added under a new id, or stated twice
nodes.description: A write that breaks a continuing relationship's identity is not refused: the board is valid, so the write lands and its answer carries RELATIONSHIP_REPLACED or RELATIONSHIP_DUPLICATED naming the repair. An explicit removeEdges plus an idless addition declares a replacement and draws no notice.

nodes.name: Adopt
nodes.responsibility: Makes a settled draft current, or gives a board nobody had built its first current variant
nodes.description: Adoption renames nothing and rewrites no history: the variant that was current becomes a historical state under its own name. On a board with no current variant nothing becomes history (ADR 0031).

nodes.name: Shelve
nodes.responsibility: Lets a proposal go without deleting it, so every link that names it still opens it
nodes.description: Shelving changes nothing the variant says; the board records that nobody intends to carry it out (ADR 0030).

nodes.name: Rename
nodes.responsibility: A pure transition that moves one name, the board's or a variant's, and keeps the old one as a former name
nodes.description: Every id, lifecycle, ancestry and record of adoption stays as it was (TASK-281, ADR 0036).

nodes.name: Former names
nodes.responsibility: Which board a name answers to: the board that carries it, else the one that used to
nodes.description: A board's own name always wins. Only a miss looks through the vault's formerNames, so a drill-down, a saved pane address or a command written before a rename keeps opening the board it meant; nothing is cached (ADR 0036).

nodes.name: Place the file
nodes.responsibility: Writes the board's file where its name puts it, moving it there first when a rename changed that name
nodes.description: A new name is taken under its own lease as well, without waiting, and refused when another board carries it or used to. A write that fails after the move puts the file back, so a refused rename leaves the vault as it was.

nodes.name: Discard
nodes.responsibility: Removes a whole board under the lease and version check a write takes, and gives back the claim it ran under
nodes.description: Used for a board made only to be recorded (TASK-304.02). A board somebody else holds is refused with the words a write gets.

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: a lease file beside the board, an agent's claim on it, and who holds it
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives in the vault, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion; a dead holder costs one lease rather than wedging the board.

nodes.name: Binding checks
nodes.responsibility: A node on the current variant whose binding names a file the repository no longer has

beats.heading: Success follows durable replacement

A move that stopped part way leaves the board in both vaults, and running it again finishes it. It gives back the claim it ran under.

nodes.name: Move preview
nodes.responsibility: Says what a move would rewrite, or why it would be refused, holding and writing nothing
nodes.description: TASK-472.16, ADR 0051. Runs the move's own checks and rewrites against the two vaults as they are on disk, then answers the board, both ends and every drill-down it would rewrite, each as it would read. A writer is never kept waiting for a question, so the answer can be out of date by the time the move runs: the move checks everything again under its leases, and the version the preview read is the one the move states.

beats.heading: Callers state a transition
beats.body: The server constructs a pure transition from a create, edit, branch, settle, adopt, shelve or rename request, and hands it to the one write boundary.

beats.heading: The aggregate changes under one lease
beats.body: The write boundary takes the board's lease, rereads the file, checks the expected version, applies semantic edits and descendant reconciliation, then validates the complete candidate before advancing its version.

beats.heading: Success follows durable replacement
beats.body: Only the validated whole-board candidate reaches the file, moved first when its name changed; file and directory fsync complete before the applied result returns.

beats.heading: An old name keeps opening the board
beats.body: A rename keeps the old name as a former name and moves the file in the same write. Reads and writes ask which board a name answers to, so a link or a claim made under the old name reaches the board without any other board changing.

beats.heading: Letting a board go is a write too
beats.body: A discard takes the same lease and version check a write does, unlinks the file durably, and gives back the claim it ran under, so a board somebody changed meanwhile is kept.
